text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.79% today as oil prices slipped following news that diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran may be progressing—specifically reports that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if military pressure eases. Refiners like MPC profit when oil prices are high and supplies are tight; the prospect of restored Iranian oil shipments and reduced geopolitical risk weakened that tailwind. The stock had surged from $410 to nearly $425 over the prior three trading days on escalating Middle East tensions, so today's pullback reflects traders taking some chips off the table as those risks appear to be thawing.

The broader pressure comes from a week of whipsaw geopolitics. U.S. oil has already fallen from above $107 to test below $100 as the market prices in the possibility of more stable supply, even though global oil still sits well above that at $130 per barrel. Refineries are running near capacity at 96.8%, so MPC's near-term margins depend heavily on crude costs staying elevated—a de-escalation scenario is headwind for that equation.
